newsitem.title: USA: NYSE weekly program trading averages 8.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: NYSE weekly program trading averages 8.5 pct.

text.p: The New York Stock Exchange said program trading averaged 8.5 percent of its average daily volume of 388.4 million shares, or 33.2 million shares, for the week of September 9-13.
Of the average 33.2 million shares during the week, buy programs accounted for an average 18.9 million shares, while sell programs accounted for an average 14.3 million daily.
In all markets, program trading averaged 43.3 million shares a day during the week of March 9-13.

Of the five member firms reporting the most program activity on the New York Stock Exchange, Morgan Stanley, First Boston and Lehman Brothers conducted most of their program activity for their own accounts. First Options and Interactive Brokers executed all of their program activity for customers.

Program trading executed by firms as agent, for non-member customers, amounted to 63.1 percent during the week, while volume executed as principal, for their own accounts, amounted to 33.1 percent of program volume from March 25-29.

Between September 9 and September 13, 24.7 percent of program trading volume executed by NYSE member firms was related to index arbitrage, while another 21.1 percent involved other derivative product-related strategies.
Program trading encompasses trading strategies involving the sale or purchase of a basket of at least 15 stocks with a value of $1 million or more the exchange said.
